newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight rates dip in liquid market.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight rates dip in liquid market.

text.p: * Central Bank opens reverse repos, T-bill windows
Manila overnight money slipped further on Wednesday to an average of 10.8125 from 10.90625 percent amid ample liquidity in the market, traders said.
"It's really flat," said a dealer, adding that the average was just 1/16 above the Central Bank's overnight borrowing rate of 10.75 percent.
"There's a lot of money in the system. There's no paper to get into," he added.
The Central Bank suspended its weekly Treasury bill auction on Monday due to the holidays for the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.
The Central Bank's term reverse repos and special series T-bills window, which was closed since last Friday because of the APEC holidays, was reopened early on Wednesday.
But despite its reopening, the market is expected to remain liquid due to maturities of 5.1 billion in T-bills at midweek, traders said.
Done rates ranged from 11.25 to 10.78125 percent, with 22 lenders and 19 borrowers.
Turnover fell to 11.821 billion from 17.384 billion pesos.
In the secondary market for T-bills, there were more buyers because of the liquidity, traders said.
"Rates dropped a lot more," said a dealer.

The three-month bills had bid rates ranging from 11.55 to 11.70 percent compared with the previous day's 11.60 to 11.875; the six months had 12.25 to 12.30 versus 12.20 to 12.425; and the one year had 12.625 to 12.75 from 12.75 to 12.80, dealers said.
